paras: The Nahunta swamp lynching was the reported killing in October 1903 of an unnamed Black man by a posse near Nahunta, after a justice of the peace had discharged him on a charge of attempted assault. According to the Dawson News, the posse took him to a swamp, where "it is said" they gave him a "new trial" from which "he never came clear." The episode is known from that single hearsay item, and the man's death is implied rather than stated.

On a Friday, probably October 23, a Black man was accused of attempting to assault Mrs. Pat Herb on George Lee's place, two miles below Hickox, near Nahunta; she escaped to Lee's house. The man was caught and tried, and Justice Johns at Hickox let him go "for want of evidence." Later a posse "re-arrested" him and carried him off to the swamp. "It is said they gave him a new trial there and he never came clear," the paper reported, giving no date of death, no place beyond "the swamp" and no names of posse members.
No report of a body, an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The only account appeared on October 28 in the Dawson News, a Georgia paper, under the headline "ANOTHER SWAMP TRIAL." and the deck "Charged With Attempted Assault and was Discharged by Court." The item set the court's discharge of the man beside the posse's swamp "new trial," using that phrase as a euphemism for the killing, and offered no comment on either. Its opening words, "Another attempted assault," and the headline's "Another" placed the case in a series, though the item names no earlier one. No wire report of the swamp killing and no Black-press account of it was found.

reader.title: Nahunta swamp lynching
bases: A posse seized a Black man whom a justice had discharged for want of evidence, carried him to a swamp and, by report, gave him a 'new trial' from which 'he never came clear' (A5).

The only report says, as hearsay, that a posse took the discharged man to a swamp for a 'new trial' and 'he never came clear', which implies but does not state a killing; the posse acted against a court's discharge on an accusation of attempted assault, under a mock 'trial' (A5). The posse's size is not given.
One short item in a Georgia weekly, itself qualified by 'It is said', is the only report found; no wire story, local paper or Black-press account was found (A5).

accounts.label: Dawson News item (hearsay)
accounts.gist: A Black man accused of attempting to assault Mrs. Pat Herb was discharged by Justice Johns for want of evidence; a posse re-arrested him and took him to the swamp, where 'it is said' they gave him a new trial and he never came clear.

framing.detail: The Dawson News headlined it 'ANOTHER SWAMP TRIAL.', noted that the court had discharged the man for want of evidence, and described the posse's action with the ironic euphemism of a 'new trial' from which 'he never came clear', without comment or condemnation.

record_check.dossier: No article names a county; the only report names Nahunta and Hickox without a county or state.
Georgia is inferred (Georgia-news page of a Georgia weekly; wire places Nahunta in Georgia), not stated in the report.
The killing is implied, not stated, and is hearsay ('It is said ... he never came clear'); no body, inquest or second report found. 'Completed' is an inference.
'Friday' is the day of the attempted assault (probably Oct. 23); the date of the seizure and killing is not given.
Near Nahunta: George Lee's place, two miles below Hickox; the man was taken 'off to the swamp'.
Supported: 'a posse re-arrested the negro'; size and members not given.

info: The attempted assault occurred on a 'Friday', most likely Oct. 23, 1903, in the week before the Oct. 28 issue; the date of the seizure and the swamp 'trial' is not given.
On George Lee's place, two miles below Hickox, near Nahunta; the man was tried at Hickox and carried 'off to the swamp'.
Accused of attempting to assault Mrs. Pat Herb, who escaped to Lee's house.
A posse, unnamed, which 're-arrested' him after his discharge.

sources.note: Only report: 'ANOTHER SWAMP TRIAL.' Unnamed Black man accused of attempted assault on Mrs. Pat Herb, discharged by Justice Johns at Hickox, re-arrested by a posse and carried to the swamp; 'he never came clear.'

set_aside: Waycross dispatch of Oct. 15: unnamed 50-year-old white woman blinded with pepper and raped near Nahunta by an unknown Black man; places Nahunta on the Brunswick and Western Railroad, twenty miles below Waycross.
Same Waycross wire on the pepper assault near Nahunta; unknown assailant, searchers without a clue.
Short rewrite of the pepper-assault wire ('The Most Horrible Yet'), dated 'Thursday near Nahunta, Ga.'
Verbatim reprint of the Manning Times item on the pepper assault.
